title.en: Python for Data and AI Work

tagline: Read, trace and debug Python by hand, then write small typed functions that grow into a command-line tool that reruns
description: Participants write Python the way data and AI work needs it: small typed functions over collections and files, errors that fail loudly, and code moved out of notebooks into scripts that rerun. The case is a fictional regional water utility with synthetic meter readings in comma-separated values (CSV) files and bilingual service tickets in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Lines. Each day opens with an AI-off drill in reading, tracing or debugging code by hand, and the labs grow into a command-line tool that validates readings, flags anomalies and writes a summary report. Arabic text normalisation and SQL are left to FN-104, version control to FN-102.
audience: Beginners. Graduates and career changers entering the AI Engineering or Data Science track; computing and data graduates who pass the placement test skip the courses it covers.
prerequisites: Has written and run a short program in any language, or completed the guided pre-work on values, conditions and loops

outcomes.text: Explain what a short program prints, step by step, including name binding, shared mutable lists and dictionaries, and scope, given ten unseen snippets on paper, without a computer or assistant
outcomes.evidence: a trace sheet with at least eight of ten outputs correct

outcomes.text: Distinguish when a notebook, a script or an importable module is the right home for a piece of code, given four tasks described by the utility's analysts
outcomes.evidence: a choice and a one-line reason per task, matching the reference on three of four

outcomes.text: Implement typed functions that load, validate and aggregate records with lists, dictionaries, sets and comprehensions, given a month of meter readings with missing, duplicated and out-of-range values
outcomes.evidence: a module that passes the provided tests and a type checker with no errors

outcomes.text: Apply exception handling and input validation so that each bad record is reported with a reason instead of crashing or passing silently, given a ticket file with malformed lines, mixed Arabic and English text and a wrong encoding
outcomes.evidence: a rejection log that accounts for every input line

outcomes.text: Use a repeatable debugging method: reproduce, shrink the input, form a hypothesis, test it, fix, and add a regression check, given three seeded defects in the course codebase, with AI assistance off
outcomes.evidence: a debugging log per defect and a passing regression test for each

outcomes.text: Prepare a command-line tool from an exploratory notebook, with an entry point, arguments and a written report, given the utility's analysis notebook and raw files
outcomes.evidence: a script that rebuilds the same report from raw files with one command on two runs

case_study.name: Manahil Water Services
case_study.summary: Manahil Water Services is a fictional regional water utility with 600 meters in six districts. Its metering team checks a month of daily readings (a CSV file with missing, repeated, out-of-range and unknown-meter rows) and its customer care team works a queue of service tickets in Arabic and English (JSON Lines). Every lab works on these files and the labs grow into Miqyas, a command-line tool that validates the readings, flags anomalies and writes a report; all data is synthetic and the same on every machine.

format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Read before you write

sessions.title: Values, names and references
outcomes: Trace a short program line by line with a table of names and objects
Predict when two names share one mutable object and when they do not

lab.title: Trace eight snippets
lab.summary: Trace eight snippets on paper, then check each answer in a step visualiser.

steps.text: Build the workspace and open the lab folder
Predict the output of all eight on paper
Step through each wrong one in a visualiser
Note what you misread; run the check

lab.stretch: Change one line of snippet 7 so that both grids print the same, and predict before you run

sessions.summary: Names bind to objects, assignment never copies, and a shared list changes for every name that holds it

sessions.title: Functions with clear contracts
outcomes: Split a script into functions that each do one job
State a function's inputs and output in its signature and docstring
Explain what a function can see and change, using scope and the call stack

lab.title: Split a script into four functions
lab.summary: Split a 40-line script into four functions with stated inputs and outputs.

steps.text: Run the script and mark its four jobs
Move each job into a function with a docstring
Put the script part under a main guard
Run the tests and the check

lab.stretch: Add a doctest to bill for a month of exactly 15 cubic metres and run it

sessions.summary: One job per function, inputs and outputs stated, effects kept at the edge, and scope explained by the call stack

sessions.title: Type hints and a checker
outcomes: Annotate parameters and return values with built-in types

Handle a value that may be None before using it

lab.title: Annotate the reading parser

steps.text: Run the tests and the checker on the supplied parser
Fix each error the checker reports

lab.stretch: Replace the tuple with a NamedTuple so that reading[2] becomes reading.m3

sessions.summary: Type hints as promises a checker verifies: built-in generics, None as a value that must be handled, and reading the checker's report

sessions.title: Parsons problems
outcomes: Order the lines of a function so that each name is bound before it is used
Use indentation to say which lines belong to a branch, a loop or a try
Reject a distractor by saying what it would do

lab.title: Rebuild a validation function
lab.summary: Reorder scrambled lines, with distractors, into a working validation function.

steps.text: Order the warm-up on paper, then in the editor
Order and indent the validation function
Run the tests; fix order or indentation
Say why each distractor is wrong; check

lab.stretch: Write one more distractor for a neighbour and say which test catches it

sessions.summary: Rebuilding a function from its scrambled lines: order, indentation, and the lines that do not belong

capstone.summary: A command-line tool that loads, validates and reports on a new synthetic dataset, the utility's maintenance work orders, submitted as a public repository whose README shows the command and its report, then a ten-minute walkthrough with a change the assessor requests
capstone.submission: A link to a public repository that holds the tool, its tests and a README that shows the one command and the report it writes on the supplied work-order files, and that states what the tool does not check. The commit history is part of the evidence. Then a ten-minute live walkthrough: the participant runs the tool, makes a change the assessor requests and explains a traceback the assessor chooses; the questions are inside the ten minutes.
